📖 **[Full design article (WeChat, in Chinese)](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/nibHYWmDTf6TkNhPhtvFdw)** — the Nüwa Test, the three-capability foundation, 18 iterations, emergence, and the taggant proposal.
**English** | [中文](README.zh-CN.md)
**⚠️ AUTHORIZED SECURITY TESTING ONLY — see [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md).**
## Meet sapper in 60 seconds
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1560dc0c-2c92-42b8-a42f-698848fb5878
🎬 中文版：[中文宣传片](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f300280a-4597-40a3-b036-8f235fbee00e)
## What this is (and isn't)
**sapper is a multi-agent orchestration harness, not a single agent.** It does
not bind to any specific AI model or CLI — you can freely swap the agent and
model behind every role:
| What you can swap | How | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Agent CLI** | `nuwa spawn --agent  ` or env var | Claude Code / Codex / Code Buddy / DeepSeek / any interactive CLI |
| **Model** | `--model` flag or `SAPPER_MODEL` env | GLM-5.3 / DeepSeek V4.1 Flash / Claude Sonnet / any model |
| **Role composition** | freely defined in the doctrine | commander on one model, soldiers on another, scouts on a third |
sapper's value is not in any single agent, but in the **mechanism for
orchestrating multiple agents to work as a coordinated force**: scheduling,
division of labor, communication, shared memory, self-healing. Swap out every
agent and model — the mechanism still works.
**This project is designed for competition scenarios** (Tencent Intelligent
Attack-Defense Challenge CTF). If you want to use this mechanism in your own
scenario (office, research, engineering, any long-horizon cooperative work):
- **Start from [nvwabase · the Nüwa Foundation](https://github.com/N1nEmAn/nvwabase)** — the general-purpose base with all three capabilities, no pentest doctrine, ready for you to iterate your own division of labor
- **Or fork this project** — but the doctrine is NOT the only thing to change; the environment wiring must change too:
  - `docker/commander/SKILL.md` (the 426-line doctrine) → your scenario's strategy
  - `BENCHMARK_BASE_URL` and related platfor

top10.descricao_en: An agent skill that finds where a photo was taken — OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite imagery and street view — and shows its work. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot.
top10.readme:
# 🧭 geo-sleuth
**An agent skill that finds where a photo was taken — and shows its work.**
   Works with  
    …and any other agent that reads  SKILL.md  and runs shell commands. 
*No text. No plates. No landmarks. One bridge, one mountain. Located to within 2 m.*
---
## Quick start
```bash
npx skills add Oldcircle/geo-sleuth
```
Pick your agents when prompted. Then hand your agent a photo and say:
> find where this photo was taken
On first use, ask the agent to run `doctor.py` from the installed skill’s `scripts/` folder and address any failed checks (see [Requirements and setup](#requirements-and-setup)). That is the whole interface. The agent reads `SKILL.md`, runs the scripts, and comes back with the camera position, the direction it was facing and a satellite evidence image. Prefer to copy the folder yourself? See [Installation](#installation).
## Why geo-sleuth
- **One photo, one sentence.** Give your agent a photo and say *find where this photo was taken*. You get back the camera position, the direction it was facing, and a satellite evidence image.
- **It works when there is nothing to read.** No sign, no plate, no landmark: OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation data, satellite tiles and street view carry the search on their own.
- **Geometry instead of guesswork.** Pier spacing becomes a distance ruler, shadows become a bearing, a ridge line becomes a fingerprint that elevation data can be matched against.
- **Every claim points at a file.** A conclusion has to name the command that ran in the session and the file it produced. Population and fame are not evidence.
- **Scripts rank, the model judges.** Twenty single-purpose scripts search, score and sort; the model only picks among the top few.
- **One skill, every agent.** A standard Agent Skill — `SKILL.md` plus plain Python scripts — so the same folder runs in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot.
- **Answers carry an error radius.** Coordinates ± radius, the camera heading, an evidence image and a graded confidence.
## Cases
None of these photos had GPS data. Each case lists what the skill read from the photo, how it narrowed the search, and how far the result landed from the confirmed camera position.
Each case is a record of one run by one model. The skill tells the agent how to work; what to query, how to filter and how many top results to check are the model's own decisions, so a different model or different decisions may not reach the same result. Under each case

# OpenBot
[ ](https://github.com/nightly-labs/openbot/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[ ](LICENSE)
OpenBot is a local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates. It supports the local
[Codex App Server](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server) and
[Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview), plus [Grok CLI](https://docs.x.ai/build/overview),
OpenCode, Gemini, [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli), [Cline CLI](https://cline.bot/cli), [Kimi Code CLI](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-cli),
[Devin CLI](https://cli.devin.ai), [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli), [Mistral Vibe](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-vibe), and [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com) through ACP. It gives every agent its own workspace and
conversation, and provides local queues, file transfers, an embedded browser, and agent-to-agent
messaging in one desktop app.
OpenBot is ready for production use. A new release ships almost every day.
> [!WARNING]
> Agents run with `danger-full-access` and `approvalPolicy: never`. They can read and modify files,
> run commands, use the network, and control the embedded browser without per-action confirmations
> after the explicit first-launch consent.
> Run only agents and tasks you trust, keep backups, and review [Security](#security) before use.
## What works
- Prompt-driven agent creation and editing on desktop and mobile, with editable instructions, avatar, and section review before saving.
- Persistent agents backed by independent Codex, Claude, Grok, OpenCode, Gemini, Cursor, Cline, Kimi, Devin, GitHub Copilot, Mistral, or Hermes sessions and local workspaces.
- Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints and custom ACP agents, with detection of local model servers (Ollama, LM Studio) and installed agents.
- Per-agent context monitoring with automatic compaction before long threads exhaust the model window.
- FIFO message queues with pause, resume, cancellation, and crash-safe persistence.
- Agent-to-agent messages, replies, reactions, images, and managed file transfers.
- Shared desktop channel chats with one task owner, explicit delegation, shared history, and Stop, Resume, Reassign, Archive, and Restore controls.
- A persistent embedded browser that agents can open, inspect, and control.
- Optional Computer Use on macOS, Windows and Linux through the `cua-driver` binary in the release, which OpenBot starts as its own child process and gives to every provider.
- Per-agent model, reasoning, pr

 Andee 
 Anything you can do, it can — and it becomes the soul of the device. 
   Not the assistant that helps you operate your phone — not a tool, not a companion.  
  What moves in is not an app on the phone.   
  A phone, a Mac, a tablet — each is a body it lives in. And the Andees on different devices can be **friends**.  
  No root. No custom ROM.  One APK on Android, one app on the Mac.   
## Andee is a personal agent
Tell it what you want. It does it on your phone and on your Mac, the way you would: it opens the app, taps, types,
reads the screen. When a job is long, it hands it to a helper and keeps talking to you. It remembers you, and it
keeps working when you are not asking.
This is the shape DeepSeek calls a [Super Agent](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype): one agent
that talks to you and keeps track of everything, and helpers that go off and do the long work. DeepSeek built theirs for a
team's GitHub repository and says it is a research prototype. Andee is the same idea for one person, on the
devices they already use.
| | **Andee** | OpenClaw | ChatGPT dots | Gemini on the phone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Runs on | your own phone and Mac | your own Mac, Windows or Linux | OpenAI's cloud, each with its own cloud computer | Google's cloud |
| Works in any phone app, without the app doing anything | **Yes** | not stated | not stated | only supported apps, a few phones, US and Korea, beta |
| Works your computer | **Yes** | files, shell, browser | can link one computer | no |
| Remembers you between chats | **Yes**, in a notebook that stays on your device | yes | yes | not stated |
| Acts when you have not asked | **Yes**, with an off switch | not stated | not stated | recurring tasks |
| Hands long jobs to a helper while you keep talking | **Yes** (works from the Mac; phone to Mac not yet tested on a device) | not stated | not stated | not stated |
| Open source | Yes | Yes | No | No |
"Not stated" means their own pages do not say. It does not mean they cannot. The other columns come from
